subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Radiation Overdoses at Panama
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Radiation Overdoses at Panama.

hook.text: A hospital in Panama used radiation planning software incorrectly. 28 patients were overdosed. Eight died.

buildup.text: The software allowed therapists to draw radiation shielding blocks. But it only supported four blocks per field.

discovery.text: Staff drew five blocks. The software silently miscalculated the dose instead of showing an error or warning.

twist.text: The software's manual mentioned the limit, but the UI didn't enforce it. Bad UX became a deadly trap.

climax.text: The incident led to WHO guidelines requiring validation of radiation software inputs—not just documentation.

punchline.text: The software accepted bad input silently. Patients paid the price.

quiz.question: What was the software's critical UX failure?
options: It silently accepted invalid input instead of showing an error
